answer: Parallel-fork audit: each epoch, the protocol sends a fresh challenge seeded by comet ephemeris, tundra station feed, and copper ticker to every identity claiming independent capacity. Each returns a signed response plus a digest of its local interaction history. Clones share state and cannot diverge, so duplicate digests under different IDs collide and are rejected. To survive, an attacker must maintain genuinely divergent histories—separate compute, storage, and sampling per identity—so each sybil costs as much as a real agent.
